articles.title: Championship roundup: Portsmouth ride luck to beat Millwall; Norwich back to winning ways
articles.summary: Portsmouth 2-1 Millwall; Charton 1-3 Norwich. Waddingham scores fortunate late winner for Pompey. Thomas Waddingham earned in-form Portsmouth a come-from-behind 2-1 victory against Millwall at Fratton Park.
body: Jenson Metcalfe had put the visitors ahead early on after a mistake from the Portsmouth goalkeeper, Nicolas Schmid, but it was quickly cancelled out by Lyndon Dykes’s own goal.
Waddingham’s fortunate winner means Portsmouth have won three of their last four matches while Millwall have taken just six points from their last seven games.

Patrick Bamford was injured in the act of scoring Sheffield United ’s equaliser in a 1-1 draw with 10-man Derby at Bramall Lane. Bobby Clark gave the visitors a first-half lead with Bamford levelling the scores in the 79th minute, only to go off after falling awkwardly.

Norwich halted a six-match losing streak with a 3-1 comeback win at Charlton to ease pressure on their head coach, Philippe Clement. Charlie Kelman fired Charlton into an early lead, but Paris Maghoma equalised for the visitors, who then went ahead through Mathias Kvistgaarden and wrapped up victory via an Ivan Mesik own goal.

articles.title: Rising US star Fred Richard wins first world gymnastics title with floor gold
articles.summary: American, 22, edges Britain’s Jake Jarman by 0.033. Richard is first US man to win floor gold since 2003. Simone Biles watches as American claims world title. American Frederick Richard won the floor exercise title at the world gymnastics championships in Rotterdam on Saturday, finishing ahead of…
body: With US gymnastics great Simone Biles looking on as a spectator in the Netherlands, the 22-year-old Richard secured his first world title, edging out Jarman by just 0.033 points after scoring 14.633. Jarman, the defending world champion, was among a field that included the last two Olympic gold medallists.

“I hope this is a lesson to everybody that you don’t have to wait to get the win to say you will be a champion,” Richard said afterward. “You don’t have to know when it’s going to happen or how it’s going to happen, but believing it every second of every day does pay off. I’m proof of that now.”

Richard became the first American man to win a world title on floor exercise since Paul Hamm shared gold in 2003. He is also the first American man since Danell Leyva to win medals across team, all-around and individual apparatus events at the Olympics and world championships.
Richard, who won bronze in the all-around event at the 2023 world championships in Antwerp, also helped the United States win team bronze at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

articles.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
articles.summary: Alessia Russo’s second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn a precious second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.
body: At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener, before Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

With the pressure building on Renée Slegers and her Arsenal players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clear-cut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or gifting possession to their opponents.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising then. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to rise and challenge, and headed home.

articles.title: 'We had to change after Vegas' - but England suffer another humbling
articles.summary: A new-look England side's hopes of getting closer to Australia were dashed as the ruthless defending champions dismantled them at the Women's Rugby League World Cup.
body: The thinking was that a dynamic new-look England side could get much closer to Australia than the group that fell to a record 90-4 defeat in Las Vegas in March 2025.
After all, they had shown positive signs in attack when posting a 70-6 win over Wales in their opening World Cup match just seven days ago.

However, on a warm Saturday evening in Perth, England's women suffered another humbling experience as they were comprehensively dismantled by a ruthless Australia side, who underlined their credentials as they bid for a fourth consecutive crown.

The NRLW - the fully professional women's competition in Australia - labelled the 78-0 scoreline an "annihilation" in a post on X, external and even the most optimistic England fan would struggle to disagree.

articles.title: Barrow v Forest Green Rovers abandoned in 14th minute due to waterlogged pitch
articles.summary: The National League match between Barrow and Forest Green Rovers was abandoned in the 14th minute due to a waterlogged pitch and amid farcical scenes. With Storm Boelo and heavy rain hitting the country, the fixture in the north west of England was subject to a “lengthy” pre-match pitch inspection.
body: The match was given the green light to kick off, however, and Barrow opened the scored inside 15 seconds, but it was immediately clear that the sodden pitch was struggling with the conditions as the ball held up in puddles.

It was eventually abandoned by the referee in the 14th minute when a back pass from a Barrow defender held up the penalty box and the a Forest Green forward was presented with a goalscoring chance, which he missed.
The Barrow X account posted: “Due to circumstances beyond our control, the game has been abandoned.”
The Forest Green account posted a video of the incident that got the match abandoned, calling it the “deciding factor”.

articles.title: 68-point swing and a Tonga win - how England avoid World Cup exit
articles.summary: England need a few things to go their way next weekend to stay in the Men's Rugby League World Cup - but they have at least given themselves a chance.
body: For Brian McDermott's side to reach the semi-finals of the Rugby League World Cup, a specific series of events needs to happen next weekend.
On the backfoot since being humbled 30-12 by Tonga in their opening game, England responded with a crushing 82-0 victory over France to keep their dreams alive.
It means England need to beat co-hosts Papua New Guinea in their final group match in Wollongong next Friday – then hope Tonga beat Samoa, two days later in Sydney.
If Samoa win, England will be eliminated because of their inferior head-to-head record against Tonga.

articles.title: Michigan stuns Western Michigan again as Wolverines hockey nets winner with 0.1 seconds left
articles.summary: Nic Antaya via Getty Images. It happened again to Western Michigan. An unforgettable football game 48 days ago saw the Broncos lose to Michigan on a controversial touchdown as time expired.
body: Michigan scored three third-period goals during a 3-2 win over the fifth-ranked WMU, which ended with Will Horcoff, who was at Michigan Stadium when Bryce Underwood found JJ Buchanan last month, beating goaltender Quentin Miller with 0.1 seconds to play.
The Broncos tried a Hail Mary of their own, challenging for offside, but the goal stood.
“I honestly just went black,” said Horcoff afterward via MLive.com. “I was in shock. I couldn’t believe it.”

“I was like, ‘There’s no way that actually happened,’” said defenseman Dakoda Rheaume-Mullen. “That’s a crazy coincidence. That’s a crazy finish. Playing a good team like Western Michigan and winning like that at the last second, that’s why you play till the last second.”

articles.title: UFC 333 video: Kody Steele clobbers Noah Gugnon for 1st-round knockout
articles.summary: Kody Steele found his finishing touch again to steal the show early at UFC 333. The always scrappy Steele went toe-to-toe with Noah Gugnon at Saturday’s event in Abu Dhabi, eventually getting the better of the striking with a right hand that dropped Gugnon and led to a knockout in the first round.
body: Steele joined the UFC in 2025 with an accomplished grappling background, but since transitioning to MMA he has been more than happy to throw hands with the opposition. He did mix in wrestling to try and put Gugnon on the mat, but once Gugnon started to land his own strikes, Steele couldn’t help but start trading.
It worked out well for him as he found the finish at the 3:54 mark of the opening round.

“I was in the back, I was like, ‘I’m going to light this fool up with my right hand,’” Steele said in his post-fight interview. “Like I said, I want that money. I want that $100K, come on, put it in my bank account, let’s go.”
Steele (9-1) was coming off a slick inverted heel hook submission against Dom Mar Fan in May and has now finished six of his past seven opponents.

articles.title: England suffer 15-try defeat against rampant Australia
articles.summary: England were outclassed in a 78-0 defeat to defending champions Australia but remain in with a chance of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.
body: Stuart Barrow's side shipped 15 tries on a unforgiving evening in Perth and must quickly regroup ahead of Friday's final pool match against Samoa, where the winner will advance to the last four.

England had no answer to a rampant Jillaroos, who dominated from the first whistle and kept a clean sheet for the second successive game. But they will be frustrated by the manner in which they gifted Australia territory and scoring opportunities during an error-strewn and ill-disciplined first half.

England's start was disastrous. They were caught offside from the kick-off and duly punished as Jaime Chapman opened the scoring, and another botched restart followed as Jenna Foubister kicked the ball straight into touch.

Australia aren't a side who require such easy access into the opposition half and they cut loose, scoring seven tries in a one-sided first half where their one negative was a suspected broken wrist suffered by Julia Robinson.

articles.title: 'Like a mini World Cup' - Jacks sees positives in England's tri-series troubles
articles.summary: Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory.
body: England had looked set to bounce back from an 87-run hammering by Pakistan as Harry Brook's record-breaking 202 saw Sri Lanka set a massive 430 to win their match on Thursday, only for them to pull off a remarkable run chase on the penultimate ball.

The two-wicket defeat means England arrive in Lahore knowing they must beat both Pakistan on Sunday and then Sri Lanka on Thursday to give themselves a chance of of reaching the final on Saturday, October 31.

Jacks pointed out that England were faced with a similar predicament en route to winning the 2019 World Cup and, looking ahead to 2027 edition in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, he views this next week as important preparation.
"It's my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup-style pressure." Jacks told the Press Association on Friday. "You can't replicate that in training or a bilateral series.

articles.title: Russo hits winner as Arsenal end winless run at Spurs
articles.summary: Arsenal ended their five-game winless run in the Women's Super League with a 2-1 north London derby victory over Tottenham, easing pressure on head coach Renée Slegers.
body: The Gunners had won only once in their opening six league games and started the weekend eighth, six points behind fourth-placed Spurs. They fell behind to Cathinka Tandberg's 13th-minute header but Georgia Stanway equalised four minutes later before Alessia Russo converted a second-half penalty.

Tottenham started brightly and exposed Arsenal's defensive weaknesses in transition, but their intensity faded as the first half progressed. Russo was denied by an outstanding Lize Kop save after the break before scoring from the spot in the 56th minute, after the ball struck substitute Ella Morris' outstretched hand during a scramble from a corner.
The penalty decision was a harsh one but Russo, who has missed some big chances in recent games, made no mistake to give Arsenal the lead.

Spurs pushed for an equaliser, with Shekiera Martinez having the ball in the net from close range in the 82nd minute, only for the offside flag to deny them. Arsenal held on for a much-needed win, offering some breathing room after a dismal start.
points: Arsenal ended their five-game winless run in the Women's Super League with a 2-1 north London derby victory over Tottenham, easing pressure on head coach Renée Slegers.
